turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the token just before a period that sits inside a token sequence and does not end a sentence. This covers decimal points (-0.07, 47.5, 29.9), domain dots (www., github.com), code member access (classList., params.), and abbreviations (N.C., U.S., i.e., A. actinomycetemcomitans).
turn1.evidence: Nearly every marked token is immediately followed by a '.' that joins two pieces, across math, law citations, URLs, JavaScript/Ruby, file paths and abbreviations. The weaker hits ('recognized.The', 'have.', 'gaming.') are ordinary or unspaced sentence-final periods, which fits the same predict-a-period feature at lower strength.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on tokens followed by other punctuation (commas, colons, slashes) and on cases where a period was likely but absent, to tell whether the unit predicts the dot itself or responds to the actual next token.
